summary: The candidate adds six relevant unified-memory cache scenarios, but its 1e-9 averaged-KL tolerance accepts nonzero KL and therefore does not implement the original issue's exact-zero correctness oracle. End-to-end Inkling execution is also unverified on the assigned AMD gfx950/ROCm host.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate collected 24 tests, including baseline, prefill-cache-hit, and decode-cache-hit cases for both Python and Rust unified radix tree backends. This measured discovery only.
Independent adversarial oracle test. Unequal logprobs produced nonzero avg_kl_div=5.0000069648240756e-11, but the candidate's exactness threshold accepted it.
Failing-before evidence on recorded base: the candidate's unified-memory class does not exist. This establishes addition of coverage, not behavioral detection of a cache defect.
Assigned accelerator is AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950, with ROCm. The issue's Inkling path requires NVIDIA CUTE/FA4 and cannot be qualified here.

gpu_execution_evidence: Hardware was identified as AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950. No candidate Inkling inference or candidate regression executed on GPU.
remaining_limitations: No supported NVIDIA CUTLASS/FA4 execution measured exact-zero KL for the baseline, prefill-cache-hit, or decode-cache-hit cases.
Neither the Python nor Rust unified-memory class completed an end-to-end Inkling request in this review environment.
No real or injected unified-memory FULL, SWA, or MAMBA state-restoration defect was demonstrated failing before and passing after.
No model weights suitable for Inkling qualification were available; the tiny Llama transport fixture cannot qualify the combined architecture.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild target existed.
remaining_counterexamples: A nonzero KL of 5.0000069648240756e-11 passes because the candidate uses an averaged threshold of 1e-9, contradicting the contract that any nonzero KL is a bug.
The six new tests are collected but have no supported end-to-end Inkling result on either tree backend.
There is no revert-then-red or fault-injection evidence for unified-memory FULL, SWA, or MAMBA restoration.
